title: Premium Bonds Pay 4.35%? Why £1,000 Has a 56% Chance of Winning Nothing 🎟️💷 #shorts
description:
Put £1,000 in Premium Bonds for a year, and there's a 56% chance you win nothing.

The 4.35% prize fund rate is an average across every Bond, lifted by two £1 million jackpots a month. Leave out prizes of £1,000 and up, and the £25, £50, £100 and £500 prizes pay about 3.7% (3.74%), below the 3.75% on NS&I's own easy-access Direct Saver.

The catch: Premium Bond prizes are tax free, savings interest isn't. If you pay 40% tax on your interest (a higher-rate taxpayer above the £500 Personal Savings Allowance), 3.75% becomes 2.25%. Savings income tax rises by 2 points (to 42% for higher-rate taxpayers) from April 2027.

How it's worked out: NS&I's October 2026 draw had 137,483,797,618 eligible £1 Bonds and 6,546,849 prizes worth £498,378,775 (odds 21,000 to 1). £1,000 = 1,000 Bonds over 12 monthly draws: (1 − 1/21,000)^12,000 ≈ 56% chance of no prize.

Sources: https://www.nsandi.com/about-us/press-releases/2026/october-premium-bonds-two-millionaires-somerset-and-east-sussex · https://www.nsandi.com/about-us/press-releases/2026/boost-for-premium-bonds-including-around-308k-extra-tax-free-prizes-plus-improved-rates-four-other-nsi-savings-products · https://www.nsandi.com/products/direct-saver · https://www.gov.uk/apply-tax-free-interest-on-savings/how-much-is-tax-free · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/changes-to-tax-rates-for-property-savings-dividend-income/changes-to-tax-rates-for-property-savings-dividend-income
